definitions: To please someone or give someone joy; takes an accusative object.

examples: Es freut mich sehr, dass Sie die Einladung angenommen haben.
I am very pleased that you have accepted the invitation.
Ihr unerwarteter Erfolg freute das gesamte Team.
Her unexpected success delighted the entire team.

definitions: This, this one; indicates a person, thing, or concept close at hand, currently under discussion, or just mentioned.
The latter (gehoben); indicates the second or more recently named of two referents.
Usage note: Contrasts with jener (the former) in formal and literary writing, whereas spoken German typically contrasts demonstrative references using stress or particles such as hier and da.
examples: Dieser Roman hat mich von der ersten Seite an gefesselt.

Goethe schätzte Schiller sehr, doch dieser hegte anfangs deutliche Vorbehalte.
Goethe held Schiller in high esteem, but the latter initially harboured clear reservations.
Er schwankte lange zwischen dieser Lösung hier und jener dort drüben.
He hesitated for a long time between this solution here and that one over there.

definitions: Just, simply; expresses that a circumstance is obvious, unavoidable, or accepted as an unchangeable fact (umgangssprachlich).
Usage note: Widely used in spoken German and informal prose as a modal particle synonymous with "eben", but avoided in formal and elevated registers.
examples: Wenn der Zug Verspätung hat, müssen wir jetzt halt warten.

Es hat nicht geklappt, aber so ist das Leben halt.
It didn't work out, but that is simply life.
